Measure coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) from solar 8B neutrinos
Search for neutrinoless double beta decay of 136Xe and other rare processes

summary.plain: XENONnT is a tank of nearly six tonnes of liquid xenon deep under a mountain in Italy, watching for dark matter particles and other rare signals. It is the upgraded successor of XENON1T, has been running since 2020, and has set new dark matter limits and reported the first hint of solar neutrinos bouncing off xenon nuclei.
summary.technical: Dual-phase xenon TPC upgrade of XENON1T: 8.5 t total / 5.9 t active liquid xenon in LNGS Hall B (INFN, ~1400 m rock). Construction began Dec 2018; operation began 2020. The first WIMP-search result (2023, 1.1 t-y exposure) set a spin-independent limit of 2.58e-47 cm^2 at 28 GeV/c^2. A 2024 analysis reported the first indication (2.73 sigma) of solar 8B neutrinos via coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering.
